output.root_problem: Since August, billing dispute tickets have doubled (E-05) even though Customer Service is already answering tickets within SLA (E-01: median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) — ruling out slow response as the cause. The best-supported mechanism (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED) is that billing import validation rules changed around August, producing incorrect bills across both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types; disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL reads (1785 vs 1240, E-03), which rules out estimate-substitution/field-staffing as the dominant driver and, combined with the absence of any logged tariff change (E-04, E-06), points to an import/calculation-side billing defect as the root cause of the ticket surge.
output.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (SH-CS, CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), 2440 tickets total (E-05, E-01).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target), so tickets are being handled promptly despite the volume surge (E-01).
Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type — the majority of disputes are on bills with real, non-estimated reads (E-03).
Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts (E-02).
causal_chain: Billing import validation rules changed around August, altering how both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED meter reads are accepted into bill calculation (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE).

The altered import validation produces incorrect bills predominantly on ACTUAL-read accounts (E-03: 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills), which is inconsistent with a tariff-rate cause since no tariff changes were logged (E-04, E-06).
Incorrect bills are issued to customers at the 'bill issue' step of the meter-to-cash process (P-M2C).
Customers file dispute tickets at roughly double the prior rate starting in August (E-05: ~600/month Jun-Jul to ~1200-1260/month Aug-Sep).
Because tickets are already answered within SLA (E-01), the surge is a billing-accuracy/volume problem upstream of Customer Service, not a response-handling capacity problem.

output.summary: The initial request (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills, but investigation found tickets are already answered within SLA (E-01), so the real problem is why bills are wrong, not slow response. Evidence shows dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1200-1260/month after August (E-05), the majority of disputed bills are on ACTUAL, not estimated, reads (E-03: 1785 vs 1240), no tariff change was logged or claimed (E-04, E-06), and the ESTIMATED-read disputes trace mainly to billing import rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads rather than field/AMI read failure (E-12). This supports H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE (a billing import validation rule change around August) as the best-supported driver, while H-AUTO-AGENT-FIX and H-AMI-READ-FAULT were rejected. The release delivered the two read-only diagnostic work items that were completed (analyze_actual_read_billing_defect on DA-BILL, correlate_route_completion_with_disputes on DA-ROUTE), while confirming the specific rule change in DA-RULES and any corrective action remain undone. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds, because the DEFINE gate was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS and the critical confirmation obligation (VOB-U-RULECHANGE) is still open and out of release scope; the remaining 70-minute budget and the no-automated-writes constraint (K-BILLWRITE) and dispatch-approval constraint (K-DISPATCH) preclude completing the structural remedy within this run.
key_points: Root problem (PD-1): billing dispute tickets doubled since August even though response times are within SLA (E-01), pointing to an upstream billing-accuracy defect rather than a ticket-handling gap.

Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL reads (1785 vs 1240, E-03), ruling out estimate-substitution/field-staffing as the dominant cause and, with no logged or claimed tariff change (E-04, E-06), pointing to a billing import/calculation defect.

E-12 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes involved valid AMI reads rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not a field/AMI read failure, further supporting H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE (SUPPORTED) over H-FIELD-READ-FAULT/H-AMI-READ-FAULT (contradicted/rejected).

The original requested solution (auto-answer tickets, auto-fix billing) was rejected (H-AUTO-AGENT-FIX, CL-01 unverified) because tickets are already handled within SLA (E-01) and the fix would require automated bill writes, which K-BILLWRITE prohibits.

Release scope actually delivered: analyze_actual_read_billing_defect (DA-BILL) and correlate_route_completion_with_disputes (DA-ROUTE), both marked DONE in the plan; these are read-only diagnostic analyses, not a fix.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the DEFINE gate was a CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs, and VOB-U-RULECHANGE (confirming the specific import rule change in DA-RULES) remains OPEN and required BEFORE_RELEASE but falls outside the released scope.

Structural remedies (confirming and rolling back the faulty rule, then gated bill correction for the ~1785 ACTUAL-read disputes) are assessed as not feasible within the remaining 225/70-minute budget, so they were deferred rather than attempted.
limitations_explained: The specific billing import rule change behind the defect was never confirmed via DA-RULES; completeness of DA-RULES and health of the billing-config tool are UNKNOWN, so even a follow-up confirmation query may fail or return incomplete records.

No automated bill adjustments were made or will be made by this solution; any correction for affected customers must go through Billing Operations' existing manual process (K-BILLWRITE), since automated writes to bills are prohibited.
Handing off the defective rule for configuration correction or rollback to ORG-UTIL billing engineering/SH-BILL is an unfinished, manual ownership change, not something this release executed.

Delivery and semantic validity of the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoffs remain UNKNOWN (U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY), and the AMI/MDMS side is further blocked by a non-transient vendor access hold, so this gap could not be closed in this run.

The full structural remedy — rule rollback plus gated correction for the ~1785 ACTUAL-read disputes — could not be completed within the remaining budget (225/70 minutes), so only the diagnostic portion of the work was released.
MDMS export access for Lakeside being provisioned (SH-AMI, E-11, CL-04) is an unverified stakeholder claim, not a tool-confirmed fact, so it was not relied upon to close the AMI data-access gap.
